title: recommend-and-dispatch can start a second, different stage beside a live one (the duplicate guard is keyed by kind)
description:
## As asked

**Problem.** `POST /api/proxy/recommend-and-dispatch` can enqueue a stage of a different kind on a ticket that already has a queued or running stage run. The only server-side guard is `guardDuplicate` (`lib/dispatch-factory.js:285`). It is keyed by issue **and kind**, and it only looks back over `DUPLICATE_DISPATCH_WINDOW_MS` (5 minutes, `lib/dispatch-factory.js:93`). The routed arm (`lib/dispatch-entrance.js` `descentArm`, `RECOMMEND_STAGES` \~L1506) has no live-row check of its own. So if the model-driven stage selector picks, say, `implementation` while a `plan` or `review` run is still live, both run at once.

**Why it matters.** Two stages running on one ticket at once burn a whole run, and they can leave conflicting PRs or verdicts that a person has to untangle. LIN-1656 fixed the same-kind case. LIN-4370 (PR #2370) closed the gap only for the look-first sequence (survey-task, survey-place, scoping): while one of those steps is live, recommend-and-dispatch refuses 409 `LOOK_FIRST_IN_FLIGHT` naming the live dispatch. Every other stage still goes through the selector, which has no such check. LIN-4370's review (comment 26578c03) named this class as outside that ticket.

**Acceptance.**

* With a queued or running stage row on a ticket, `recommend-and-dispatch` without an explicit `kind` does not enqueue a different-kind stage. It refuses with a code that names the live dispatch, as `LOOK_FIRST_IN_FLIGHT` does.
* The explicit `kind` override and `force` keep working as the operator's escape.
* Autopilot coordinator rows (`kind: 'autopilot'`) do not count as live stage runs, or a ticket would wait on its own coordinator.
* A wired test goes through the real `POST /recommend-and-dispatch` handler with one live stage row and shows nothing is enqueued.

**Anchors.** `lib/dispatch-factory.js` `guardDuplicate` (L285); `lib/dispatch-entrance.js` `descentArm` (\~L1668) and `overrideArm` (\~L1557); `lib/recommendation-look-first.js` `liveRunToWaitOn` and `lookFirstWaitRefusal` (the look-first-only version of this guard); `lib/recent-runs.js` `stageRuns` (counts only `PROMPT_TEMPLATES` kinds).

**Priority:** Medium (priorityLevel 2). The class predates LIN-4370 and has not been seen to cause harm. The riskiest new path (look-first) is already guarded. But each occurrence wastes a run and can produce conflicting work, and autopilot volume makes a repeat likely.

### Unvalidated idea

Lift `liveRunToWaitOn`'s "any live stage run" branch out of the look-first route into the routed arm of `recommend-and-dispatch`, so every routed dispatch answers 409 with the live id when a stage row is live. The `loadRecentRuns` read that recommend-and-dispatch already makes carries the run ids, so no new store read is needed.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** consolidate the decision this task touches
**Why:** One rule, applied before the stage selector, refuses any new stage beside a live stage run on every recommendation surface; the look-first wait becomes one case of it, because the selector offering a stage is the cause.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** a ruling

## Implementation Plan

*Planned at* `f5b1f5efa` *(LinearViewer main). Builds on the two Surveys (comments 3fbdac8f, ecaeac7f) and the autopilot ruling* `lin4392-wait-surfaces` *(comment e2e07f09). Every claim below was re-read at HEAD.*

### What this is for, and what done looks like

**The problem, as asked:** recommend-and-dispatch can start a second stage of a different kind beside a queued or running one on the same ticket. The duplicate guard is keyed by issue and kind, and it only looks back five minutes.

**Cause.** No rule says "one live stage per ticket" before the stage selector is asked. The selector sees live runs only as a hint (`, started` in `formatRecentRuns`, `lib/recent-runs.js`), and nothing stops it picking a stage beside them. LIN-4370 added that rule for the look-first sequence only. It lives inside `lookFirstRoute`, behind `lookFirstOff` (`lib/recommendation-look-first.js`), so a ticket with a plan, a PR, a blocker, children or no As-asked block never reaches it. Those are exactly the tickets this bug is about.

**Done when** (the ticket's Acceptance, which serves as Done-when):

1. With a queued or running stage row on a ticket, recommend-and-dispatch without `kind` enqueues nothing and refuses 409 with a code that names the live dispatch.
2. The `kind` override and `force` still dispatch: they are the operator's escape.
3. Autopilot coordinator rows (`kind: 'autopilot'`) never count as live stage runs.
4. A wired test through the real `POST /recommend-and-dispatch` handler, with one live stage row, shows nothing is enqueued.

The autopilot ruling (e2e07f09) adds a fifth: GET /recommend and the task page show the same wait, so no surface offers a stage the verb would refuse.

**Cuts to the As-asked block: none.** The "Unvalidated idea" puts the check in the routed arm. This plan puts it one layer down, where run data actually exists. That is a design choice, not a cut: everything the idea wanted (409 with the live id, no new store read) is delivered. Why the arm is the wrong layer is under *Which way* below.

**Drift.** None in purpose. The rule is one step broader than the words: it also refuses a *same-kind* stage beside a live row older than five minutes. That case slipped past `guardDuplicate`'s window too, and it is the same harm.

### Which way, and why

**One live-stage rule, in** `codeRouteOf` **(**`lib/openrouter.js`**), checked first, before the review-loop bound and the look-first sequence.** If any stage run in the hop's `allRuns` is live (`isLiveRun`: queued or running), the hop answers a **wait** naming the newest live run. It sends no step, writes no prompt and makes no selector call. `codeRouteOf` already feeds every recommendation surface:

* recommend-and-dispatch, through the descent arm;
* GET /recommend, at `routes/proxy-compute.js` and `routes/proxy.js`;
* the task page's buffered GET and both of its streams, in `routes/workspace-api.js`.

So one rule covers them all. `allRuns` comes from the run read each hop already makes (`prepareRecommendationInput` → `loadRecentRuns`), so there is no new store read.

**The look-first wait folds into it.** `liveRunToWaitOn` and the wait branch of `lookFirstRoute` are deleted. Once the general rule has run, no stage run is live when look-first is reached, so that branch could only fire on a bypass. `lookFirstRoute` goes back to picking a step or standing aside. `lookFirstStep`/`lookFirstRoute` collapse to one function; the builder keeps whichever name has more callers. That leaves one rule, not two.

**Order: live wait → review-loop bound → look-first → selector.** The bound dispatches `blocked`, which is a stage kind (it is in `PROMPT_TEMPLATES`). Sending it beside a live plan-review is the very concurrency this ticket refuses. Nothing about a live run needs the bound to fire first.

**It applies on every descent hop, parents included.** A parent with a live stage run waits, and the descent does not go on into its children. This is an engineering call, for three reasons:

* the selector on a parent hop may pick the parent's own stage, the exact case to refuse, and before the selector runs, code cannot know it won't;
* the stage runs a parent carries (breakdown, plan, review) reshape the children the descent would enter;
* a wait that named nothing and let the descent through would make the read surfaces disagree with the verb.

Autopilot's fan-out calls children by their own identifiers, so siblings are unaffected. Only a descent *through* a busy parent stops, and it stops visibly, naming the parent's live dispatch.

**What counts as live.** Only `stageRuns` facts with outcome `queued` or `running`. `stageRuns` keeps only `PROMPT_TEMPLATES` kinds, so `autopilot`, `custom`, `wake`, `leftover`, `periodical` and abort rows never count. That gives acceptance item 3 by construction, and a test pins it. A row `waiting on a person`, ended, closed or aborted is not live. If the run read fails (`allRuns: null`), the rule stands aside and the selector decides, as today. A store fault must not stall every ticket, and the same-kind duplicate guard still runs at the enqueue.

**Escapes, all on the descent arm only:**

* `kind` **override:** `overrideArm` never calls `codeRouteOf`. It needs no change, only a test.
* `force: true`**:** the descent arm passes a flag through `computeRecommendation` (`routes/proxy.js`) into `getRecommendation`'s options and on to `codeRouteOf`, which then skips the live wait on every hop. This is new behaviour: today `force` does not escape LIN-4370's look-first wait. The acceptance asks for it, and the ruling repeats it. With the wait skipped, look-first sends its next unattempted step and the selector decides as before.
* `followUpTo` **set:** skips the wait the same way. A follow-up beat usually resumes the very session that is live, and refusing it would break beats (the `stepper` variant drives beats over `followUpTo`+`force`). This keeps the exemption `guardDuplicate` already gives.

GET /recommend and the task page take no bypass: they have no `force`. The flag rides in the call's options, not in the recommendation context, so it never touches `prepareRecommendationInput`. That keeps clear of the five-hand-built-contexts trap (Waiting entry on `lib/recommendation-input.js`, `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`, LIN-4393 leftovers).

**Naming: one neutral name per role, and the look-first names retire.** All consumers live in this repo, and the autopilot reads its instructions live.

| Role | Today | After |
| -- | -- | -- |
| refusal code | `LOOK_FIRST_IN_FLIGHT` | `STAGE_IN_FLIGHT` |
| response field | `lookFirstWait` | `liveWait` (same shape: `{kind, id, dispatchedAt, outcome}`) |
| trace `codeRoute` | `look-first-wait` | `live-wait` |

Each code means one action ("adopt and watch the live id"), so keeping the old code for look-first tickets would be two names for one answer. The trace-store doc comment keeps `look-first-wait` as a legacy value stored traces may carry; nothing validates or filters on it (checked: the only reader is `scripts/eval/jev-routing-eval.mjs`, which tests truthiness).

**The refusal wording is general.** It names the kind, outcome and dispatch id. It says to adopt and watch the run, and that the next step is chosen once it ends. If the run is wedged: abort it (an aborted run no longer holds the ticket, and a look-first step still counts as attempted), or send a step by hand with `kind`. It promises no look-first advancement and never mentions `force`. The builder writes the exact text.

**New home:** `lib/recommendation-live-wait.js` holds the predicate over `allRuns` (newest live stage run, or null), the code constant and the refusal builder. Its path already maps to llm-and-prompts in `docs/areas/areas.json`, so the registry needs no change. The refusal import in `lib/dispatch-entrance.js` and `routes/workspace-api.js` moves to it.

**Set aside:**

* *A check in* `descentArm` *(the ticket's idea):* `descentArm` holds only `rec`, not `allRuns`. It would still pay for a selector call, would cover one surface of three, and would leave a second copy of the rule beside look-first's.
* *Widening* `guardDuplicate` *to any kind:* that sits at the enqueue, after the selector has been paid for, and the read surfaces would still offer the stage. It also changes POST /dispatch, which a person drives with an explicit prompt.
* *A store claim ("one live stage per ticket" as compare-and-set):* this is the real invariant, but it is a new store primitive with its own failure modes ("no row yet is no guard": the LIN-4375 lesson in `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`). This plan's wait is a read. Two calls racing within milliseconds can both pass, and the same-kind guard still catches same-kind races. That residual risk is accepted, not routed around. The builder adds a Waiting entry for the claim (see *Leftovers*).
* *Changing* `formatRecentRuns`*'* `, started` *hint:* the selector now meets a live run only on a bypass, where the hint is still true. Changing it would move router snapshots for nothing.

### Every place the behaviour lives

The behaviour: *"a recommendation surface answers wait, rather than a stage, while a stage run is live on the ticket."* Each of these places either computes that answer or carries it.

**In scope:**

* `lib/openrouter.js`: `codeRouteOf` (new first route, bypass option), `codeRoutedRecommendation` (returns `liveWait`, trace `live-wait`), both seam comments.
* `lib/recommendation-look-first.js`: delete `liveRunToWaitOn`, the wait branch, `LOOK_FIRST_IN_FLIGHT_CODE` and `lookFirstWaitRefusal`. Rewrite the "Waiting on a live run" module note as a pointer to the general rule.
* `lib/recommendation-live-wait.js` (new).
* `lib/dispatch-entrance.js`: `descentArm` refuses on `rec.liveWait` and passes the bypass into `computeOne`.
* `routes/proxy.js`: `computeRecommendation` takes the bypass, forwards it, and returns `liveWait`.
* `routes/proxy-compute.js`: GET /recommend returns `kind: null` and `liveWait`.
* `routes/workspace-api.js`: the buffered field spread and `done`, the leaf stream's error, the descent stream's error.
* `lib/prompt-trace-store.js`: doc comment enum.
* `lib/proxy-instructions.js`, at the GET /recommend bullet and the LOOK-FIRST IN FLIGHT bullet: rewrite both as the general wait. Add "and the in-flight wait" to the existing `force` bullet, which already says force is not the answer to a 409. That keeps the contract true without inviting autopilot to use it.
* `lib/stage-router.js` and `lib/recommendation-facts.js` comments: "code settles only the review loop bound and the look-first sequence" becomes three routes, with the live wait first. The stage-router edit is source bytes, so it moves `STAGE_ROUTER_SOURCE_CEILING` in `tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js` with a LIN-4392 reason. The old reason goes to "Ceiling history" in `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md`; see the llm-and-prompts lesson "Prompt size is frozen". No rendered prompt changes.
* Docs: `docs/proxy-integration.md` (the 409 table row), `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md` (the code-routes paragraph), `docs/plans/survey.md` (the `LOOK_FIRST_IN_FLIGHT` mention).
* Tests: `tests/unit/lin-4370-look-first-route.test.js` keeps its look-first cases with the new code and field names, and gains the new witnesses below or a sibling `lin-4392-*` file (builder's choice). `tests/unit/recent-runs.test.js` and `tests/unit/recommendation-input.test.js` comments say "the live wait".

**Out of scope:**

* `lib/dispatch-factory.js` `guardDuplicate`: unchanged; it still backs races and POST /dispatch.
* POST /dispatch and the session lane: a person supplies the prompt and kind.
* The test-mode mock in `computeRecommendation` (`routes/proxy.js`): it never calls `codeRouteOf`, as it doesn't for look-first today. E2E in test mode sees no wait.

**How the sweep is known complete.** The grep below finds every place that names today's wait: 43 matching lines in 12 files at HEAD, all listed above. After the change it must return only the legacy note in `lib/prompt-trace-store.js`:

`git grep -n -E "lookFirstWait|look-first-wait|LOOK_FIRST_IN_FLIGHT|lookFirstWaitRefusal|liveRunToWaitOn"`

The read-surface witnesses (W7) fail on any surface that still answers a stage. W13 pins the instructions to the code constant, which closes the survey's "no test notices if the instructions drift".

**What reading cannot settle: production rows.** The witnesses cannot reach how many tickets carry a silent `taken` row today. What catches it: the wait names the dispatch id on every surface, and each wait records a `live-wait` trace. A ticket with repeated `live-wait` traces over hours is a wedged row, recovered by abort.

### Likeliest ways this breaks

1. **A silent row now stalls any ticket, not just look-first ones.** "Age alone never ends a run" (`lib/recent-runs.js`), so a `taken` row that never posts a terminal holds its ticket until someone aborts it.
   * This is deliberate: the alternative is a time-based end, which `runFact` rightly refuses.
   * The stall is visible, with the dispatch id, on all three surfaces.
   * Parked CI runs do not wedge. A run that parks `[pending]` reads `running` and holds the ticket while CI runs, which is correct: the ci-wake resumes that same session. When the lineage ends `done`/`failed`/`aborted`, the live closer in `addFeedback` (`lib/dispatch-store.js`, unflagged) stamps the parked row `lineage-terminal`, and it reads `closed`.
   * Residual risk: a lineage whose last word is a non-closing `[blocked]` or `[skipped]` on the wake row leaves the parked stage row `running`. `runFact` reads the row's own feedback, not its lineage; see the runs-and-dispatch lesson "Any session can park `[pending]` on CI…". The ticket then waits until the lineage closes or the row is aborted. Not fixed here: reading the lineage changes what the selector sees on every ticket and needs its own witnesses. Recorded as a Waiting entry.
2. **A bypass leaks or is missed.** For example: `force`/`followUpTo` reaches only the first hop; GET /recommend gains a bypass; `force` stops escaping `guardDuplicate`. Covered by W4–W6 and the unchanged LIN-2872 suite.
3. **Existing tests seed a live row on a live-path descent and expect a dispatch.** Candidates include `lin-4248-survey-dispatch-paths`, `lin-3134-*`, `lin-3136-dispatch-gate`, `chat-tools`, `lin-3805-store-fault-503` and `dispatch-entrance-no-token`. Run the full suite. A failure that expected a second stage beside a live one is a finding to read, not a fixture to bend. Report it in the PR. The LIN-2872 force/followUp suite runs in test mode with no `listItems`, so it is not expected to move.

### Witnesses

Each witness fails before the change and passes after, unless marked *guard*. Every wired test drives the real `POST /recommend-and-dispatch` or GET handler on the live path, with a `setFetchImpl` that throws if the model is asked. The template is the "while a look-first step is live" block in `tests/unit/lin-4370-look-first-route.test.js`.

* **W1 (acceptance 1 and 4):** a non-look-first leaf with a plan in its description and one silent `taken` `plan` row. No `kind`. Expect: 409 `STAGE_IN_FLIGHT`; body `id`/`kind`/`outcome`/`issueIdentifier` name that row; zero items enqueued; the model is never asked.
* **W2:** as W1, with a *queued* `review` row instead. Same 409, outcome `queued`.
* **W3 (acceptance 3, guard):** only a live `autopilot` row and a live `custom` row on the ticket. The selector is asked and the stage is enqueued (201).
* **W4 (acceptance 2, guard):** as W1 with `kind: 'implementation'`. 201, item kind `implementation`.
* **W5 (acceptance 2: the loosened guard):** `force: true`, no `kind`.
  * W1's ticket: the selector is asked, 201.
  * A look-first leaf with a silent `survey-task`: 201 with `survey-place`. This one fails today.
  * What the guard was there to stop: the same call *without* `force` on that look-first ticket still answers 409.
* **W6:** `followUpTo` set, no `kind`, live row present. Not refused by the wait.
* **W7 (the ruling):** with W1's rows:
  * GET `/api/proxy/issues/:id/recommend` → 200, `prompt`, `recommendedAction` and `kind` all null, `liveWait` naming the row;
  * the workspace buffered GET carries `liveWait`;
  * the leaf stream and a parent's descending stream each emit `event: error` with `STAGE_IN_FLIGHT` and the id, with no prompt streamed.
  * All with the model never asked.
* **W8 (order):** a leaf whose plan-review loop is exhausted (`reviewLoopStop` fires) with a live `plan-review` row. Answers wait, not `blocked`.
* **W9 (parents):** a parent with a live `breakdown` row and an open focused child. recommend-and-dispatch on the parent → 409 naming the parent's row; the child is never fetched. The existing parent-stream case (child live) keeps passing under the new names.
* **W10 (guard):** the run read throws (`allRuns: null`). No wait; the selector decides.
* **W11 (guard):** the existing wedge-recovery case. Once the silent row is aborted, the next call dispatches.
* **W12:** a same-kind live `plan` row dispatched more than five minutes ago. 409 `STAGE_IN_FLIGHT`. Today the selector re-picks `plan` and `guardDuplicate`'s window has passed.
* **W13:** `lib/proxy-instructions.js`' output contains `STAGE_IN_FLIGHT_CODE` (imported, not retyped) and does not contain `LOOK_FIRST_IN_FLIGHT`.
* A unit test of the new predicate covers live vs ended, waiting, aborted and non-stage rows, and that the newest live run is named.

### Constraints carried from history and area notes

* `lib/proxy-instructions.js` and `lib/dispatch-entrance.js` changed in LIN-4349, 4382 and 4393 since this ticket was filed (`git log --oneline -15`), but not in the wait or guard code. Rebase before editing the instructions; they move in most merges.
* llm-and-prompts lesson ("Prompt size is frozen"): the stage-router comment edit moves its source ceiling with a reason. No stage or router render changes, so no router snapshot or `scripts/eval/meta-prompt.baseline.txt` changes. If one moves, something beyond a comment changed.
* runs-and-dispatch lessons: on parks and ci-wake endings ("read the lineage"), see break 1; on read vs claim (LIN-4375), see *Set aside*.
* agent-api Waiting entry on `lib/proxy-instructions.js` hand-spelling the look-first sequence: context only. The rewritten bullet no longer lists the steps, which shrinks that entry; the builder trims or removes it in the same change if it becomes untrue.

### Leftovers (one home each, per `LEFTOVER_RULE`)

The builder adds two Waiting entries in the same change:

* to `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`, citing `lib/recent-runs.js`: "`runFact` reads a row's own feedback, so a stage run parked `[pending]` whose lineage ends on a non-closing wake marker reads `running` and holds the live-stage wait (LIN-4392)";
* to `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`, citing `lib/recommendation-live-wait.js`: "the live-stage wait is a read; two racing calls of different kinds both pass; the invariant belongs in the store as a compare-and-set claim, like `claimHeldWake` (LIN-4392, Survey global)".

### Landing

One PR in LinearViewer, in this order inside it:

1. the new module and its unit test;
2. `codeRouteOf` and the look-first fold, with the look-first suite renamed and green;
3. bypass plumbing and the descent-arm refusal;
4. the surfaces (proxy-compute, proxy.js, workspace-api);
5. the instructions, comments, docs and ceiling;
6. the full suite.

No `refactor required` was named by research. The look-first fold is part of this change, not a separate refactor. Nothing lands in simple-dispatcher.

fits one session: about ten source files plus docs. Most edits are renames that one grep checks, and the logic sits in one new function and one option thread.

This loosens a guard (`force` now escapes LIN-4370's wait) and changes the dispatch contract (a new 409 code and response field on recommend-and-dispatch and GET /recommend), so it gets a second reader.

plan-review due: yes

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4392 @ f5b1f5efa

**The ticket points at the wrong seam.** It anchors the fix in `descentArm` and says the `loadRecentRuns` read already carries the run ids. It does, but only inside `computeRecommendation`, once per descended identifier (`lib/recommendation-input.js:37`). `descentArm` never sees `allRuns`, only `rec`. LIN-4370 put its wait in `codeRouteOf` (`lib/openrouter.js:2099`), before the selector is called. From there `lookFirstWait` reaches every surface: recommend-and-dispatch (`dispatch-entrance.js:1724`), GET /recommend (`routes/proxy-compute.js:540`, `routes/proxy.js:1578`) and the task-page stream (`routes/workspace-api.js:301,377`). A guard only in `descentArm` still pays for a selector call, and the read surfaces would keep showing `implementation` beside a live `plan`. **First move: a code route in `codeRouteOf`, not a check in the arm.**

**Why it will be hard:**

1. **The live check sits behind `lookFirstOff`.** `liveRunToWaitOn`'s "any live stage" branch only runs when look-first applies. `lookFirstOff` returns early for no As-asked block, not a leaf, has a plan, has a PR, an open blocker (`recommendation-look-first.js:138`). Those are exactly this ticket's cases. The new route has to sit beside look-first, with its order relative to `reviewLoopStop` decided. Lifting the function unchanged won't work.

2. **Wedged rows will block every ticket.** "Age alone never ends a run" (`recent-runs.js` `stageRuns`): a silent `taken` row stays `running` forever. Today that stalls only look-first tickets. Afterwards, any ticket with one silent row stops until a person aborts it. That is the restrictive failure `guardDuplicate`'s doc warns against, and autopilot volume will find it.

3. **`force` doesn't escape a wait today.** The look-first wait refuses before `force` is read. `force` is checked only in `guardDuplicate`, after the descent. Meeting "force keeps working" needs new plumbing (pass `force` into the code route, or check it in the arm before the wait). That also changes LIN-4370's behaviour, so confirm it is intended.

4. **Code and docs.** `LOOK_FIRST_IN_FLIGHT`'s message and `proxy-instructions.js:918` are look-first specific ("the sequence sends the step after it"), which is wrong for a live `review`. A new code means updating the autopilot instructions and the stream's error path. Reusing the old one means rewording it.

5. **Exemptions.** A `followUpTo` beat should stay unrefused, as it is under `guardDuplicate`. Autopilot rows are already excluded: `autopilot` is in `DISPATCH_META_KINDS`, not `PROMPT_TEMPLATES`, so `stageRuns` drops it. If the guard reads `allRuns`, acceptance item 3 comes free.

**A deeper question.** The selector already sees live runs marked `, started` (`formatRecentRuns`), so the current design lets the model choose concurrency on purpose. Before removing that, check for legitimate overlap. Example: a review sent while an implementation that already opened its PR has not posted a terminal marker. If that happens, the real problem is runs that don't close promptly, and a hard refusal will cause stalls.

**Test template:** `tests/unit/lin-4370-look-first-route.test.js:468` (`rows`/`live`/`items`, `noModel()`). Use a non-look-first leaf (e.g. one with a plan) and a silent `plan` row.

## Survey global: LIN-4392 @ f5b1f5efa

**Where it lands.** Not really in `dispatch-entrance.js`. The wait LIN-4370 built is a *code route*: `codeRouteOf` (`lib/openrouter.js:2099`) runs the review-loop bound and then `lookFirstRoute`. Both recommendation seams call it, so the same answer reaches recommend-and-dispatch (`dispatch-entrance.js:1724`), GET /recommend (`routes/proxy.js:1578`, `routes/proxy-compute.js:540`) and the task-page stream (`routes/workspace-api.js:124/301/377/531`). The area is young (LIN-4370, days old) and improving: one run read, one live predicate (`isLiveRun`), one refusal builder. The weak spot is naming. `lookFirstWait`, `look-first-wait` and `LOOK_FIRST_IN_FLIGHT` are spread across ~8 call sites, and the refusal text talks about "the next step" and look-first recovery.

**Done the obvious way** (a live-row check in `descentArm`), the task would leave a second copy of the live-stage rule beside `liveRunToWaitOn`. It would cover one seam of three, so the task page would still offer the stage the verb refuses. The arm also has no `allRuns`, only `rec`. A cleaner route is a third code route in `codeRouteOf` after look-first: "any `isLiveRun` in `allRuns` → wait". Every seam gets it. Acceptance 3 is already met, because `stageRuns` counts only `PROMPT_TEMPLATES` kinds, and `autopilot`, `custom`, `wake` and `leftover` aren't among them.

Must learn of it: `proxy-instructions.js:282` and `:918` (the autopilot's only way to know what to do on the 409), `docs/proxy-integration.md:2880`, `prompt-trace-store.js:40` (codeRoute enum), `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md`, and the three `lookFirstWait` emitters in `workspace-api.js`. No test notices if the instructions text drifts.

**What it could disturb (policy questions to settle first):**
- **Parents.** The route runs on every descent hop. A parent with a live run of its own (say a `breakdown`) would stop descent into children that could go. Look-first never hit this because it is leaf-only.
